title: PSC system reference: patient pharmacy moves on Prescriptions & Renewals
content:
**Subject.** A Prescriptions & Renewals patient may move one of their own prescriptions, together with the fills it still authorizes, to a pharmacy they name. When a patient moves a prescription to a retail pharmacy, the prescription keeps its fills and its expiration date, and its per-fill days' supply at the retail pharmacy becomes the retail fill length. A move to a mail-order pharmacy is dispensed at the mail-order days' supply and is outside the retail fill length.

**Business effect of one move.** The pharmacy the prescription stands at becomes the named pharmacy, its count of pharmacy moves goes up by one, and its per-fill days' supply becomes the value recorded with the move. The fills still authorized and the last date the prescription may be filled stay as they were.

### Situation of use and capability

The tool records, for a single prescription of the patient, a move to the pharmacy the patient names and the days' supply each fill of that prescription will dispense there. One call changes that one prescription only.

### How it is invoked

The tool is `move_prescription_pharmacy_221e1a97`. It is the patient's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves (the patient) runs it. The agent does not run it on the patient's behalf.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `prescription_id` | reference number of the patient's prescription being moved, as shown by the prescription lookup for this patient | identifier |
| `pharmacy_name` | the pharmacy the patient names to receive the prescription | verbatim: exactly as the patient states it, every word, digit and punctuation mark kept, nothing added, shortened or reworded |
| `days_supply` | days' supply each fill of this prescription dispenses at the receiving pharmacy | whole number of days written as an integer greater than 0, no decimals and no unit text |

The tool has no enumerated parameters.

### Return

On success the receipt is a dictionary echoing the recorded values: `prescription_id` (the prescription moved), `pharmacy_name` (the pharmacy it now stands at, as recorded), `days_supply` (integer days per fill now recorded), `transfer_count` (integer count of pharmacy moves of this prescription, this one included) and `status`, which reads "moved" when the move is recorded. Afterwards the prescription lookup shows the new pharmacy, the new per-fill days' supply and the raised move count. No other return or error is defined for the tool.

### Illustration of the contract (hypothetical values)

A call with `prescription_id` "RX-EXAMPLE", `pharmacy_name` "Maple Street Pharmacy #12" and `days_supply` 45 returns a receipt with `pharmacy_name` "Maple Street Pharmacy #12", `days_supply` 45, a `transfer_count` one higher than before and `status` "moved". The values are placeholders for the format only.
